page: Amazon Web Services r8i.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 32-core, 64-thread Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz. The processor architecture incorporates 480 MB of shared L3 cache alongside support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets. System memory is provisioned with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz, delivering an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is rated at a 30 Gbps baseline interface. The instance does not include bundled local storage or discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded execution and high memory read performance. In Geekbench testing, the system achieves a top-tier multi-core score of 21,093.0 and a Clang software compilation score of 60,561.0. Read bandwidth for cached small blocks reaches 5,123.16 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads reach 192.43 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at 120.37 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations register at 28,496.57. For CPU-based machine learning, the integrated AMX matrix engines sustain 296.71 prompt tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks operates within an average band at 76.62 GB/sec.

The r8i.16xlarge offers high memory density and multi-core throughput, generating efficient resource utilization for architectures requiring substantial RAM relative to compute capacity. Because local storage is absent, data persistence relies on networked volumes operating over the 30 Gbps network fabric. This configuration is aligned with in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise relational database backends, large-scale software build environments, and distributed data analytics.
